summary: The first state fire tower in Langlade County stood on Nine Mile hill by July 1928; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone.

events.note: Described as the first state fire observation tower in Langlade County in a July 1928 report quoted by a lookout history site. No build date found.

evidence.supports: 1928 report: the first tower is located on Nine Mile hill in the eastern part of Langlade County
evidence.quote: The first tower is located on Nine Mile hill in the eastern part of the county.

evidence.supports: 1928 report: a second state tower was being started on Hulbert Hill
evidence.quote: Erection of a second state fire observation tower in Langlade county has been started on Hulbert hill

evidence.supports: 1928 report: the Hulbert Hill tower site is about 2.5 miles north of Bryant
evidence.quote: two and one-half miles north of Bryant

evidence.supports: Lookout history index files Nine Mile Hill under Lincoln County
FFLA lists Ninemile, Langlade County, as gone
FFLA lists a Hulbert Hill tower in Langlade County as gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A lookout history index files Nine Mile Hill under Lincoln County. The 1928 report and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list place it in Langlade County, so the story uses Langlade.

sources.title: Wisconsin - Forest Lookouts (index, with 1928 newspaper extracts)

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence. The only detail is a July 27, 1928 newspaper report (Stevens Point Daily Journal), quoted on a lookout history index, that calls Nine Mile hill the first state fire observation tower in Langlade County. No build date, staff, fires or site description found. Identity of Nine Mile hill with the FFLA point Ninemile (45.23215, -88.77215) is inferred from name and county; no coordinates for the hill were found. Budget used: 2 searches, about 4 page reads. A Langlade County Historical Society page and a Facebook post were checked and had nothing on it. Worth a human check of the original 1928 newspaper and any Wisconsin Conservation Commission records.
